what_happened: The operator measured where job time went, using the go and land logs of 33 jobs from 2026-10-23 to 25. Per landed job: producer 17.6 min, Athena's checks 9.7 min, landing 15.4 min, planning about 3 min, verifier 1.6 min. Jobs that did not land used 30% of job time (5.8 of 19.3 hours), and send-backs cost 1.3 hours. The operator then replaced the broad speed request with two narrower requests: cut A (20261025-034731-2am0), which reuses CI on unchanged governed content, and cut B (20261025-034733-c453), which builds a faster suite. No job failed. The operator did the measuring and the splitting by hand.
cause: Athena has no step that checks a request for scope and for data reachability before dispatch. It does not ask whether the producer can see the inputs the request depends on (records/ is not visible in its working copy). It does not ask whether the request holds several separable cuts. Time-per-stage measurement is also not an Athena capability, so the operator does that analysis. The closest registry classes (oversized plan, reading scope exceeds deadline, unreachable ref) each cover only part of this. They fire after a plan or reading exists, not at intake of a broad request that needs measurement first.
prevention: Add an intake check before dispatch with two parts. (1) Reachability: if a request's outcome depends on data outside the producer's working copy (records/, logs), Athena runs the measurement itself in a stage that can read it and gives the producer the result as pinned input. (2) Size: if a request has more than one separable cut, Athena splits it into one job per cut, each with its own acceptance, and records that it did so. A standing time-by-stage report (per-stage minutes per landed job, share of time in non-landing jobs) would also let such requests be written against numbers from the start.
proposed_request: Add an intake step to Athena that runs before a request is dispatched to a producer. Outcome: (1) When a request depends on data the producer's one-commit working copy cannot see (such as records/ or the go and land logs), Athena computes the needed figures in a stage that can read them and passes them to the producer as a pinned input file, and refuses to dispatch if the data is unreachable. (2) When a request names or implies several separable changes, Athena proposes one job per change, each with its own acceptance criteria, and queues them in order instead of one oversized job. Acceptance: a test with a broad 'make jobs faster' style request shows the data step is run and the request is split into separate queued jobs; a test with a single-change request shows it passes through unsplit; a test with unreachable data shows dispatch is refused with a clear message. Also add an `athena report time` command that prints minutes per stage (producer, checks, landing, planning, verifier) per landed job and the share of time spent on jobs that did not land, from the go and land logs.
